title: Corrected BMP canonical correctness at one million passages
question: Does the validated corrected BMP preserve canonical top-10 results on the nested 1M subset?
hypothesis: Both raw and compressed block-32 layouts exactly match the sequential oracle on the same 25 calibration queries.
motivation: Establish next-scale external alignment before matched performance experiments.

configuration.documents.reason: Test correctness at the next nested corpus size.

declared_changes.inputs.index: Use the preserved 1M GSP hash and original BP order. Query weights, membership/order and algorithm settings remain fixed.

query_split: first 25 calibration queries; no held-out evaluation
timing_boundary: correctness only; no comparative timing statistic
correctness_rule: Byte-identical CIFF-to-GSP and effective-query round trips; fresh gated CPU top-10 byte equality with historical reference; corrected raw/compressed outputs exactly equal all 25 canonical top-10 lists.
measurement_and_analysis_plan: Byte-identical CIFF-to-GSP and effective-query round trips; fresh gated CPU top-10 byte equality with historical reference; corrected raw/compressed outputs exactly equal all 25 canonical top-10 lists.
success_rule: Both layouts have zero exit failures and zero ordered-ID/score differences for all 25 queries.
failure_rule: Retain any failed attempt and discrepancy before a reviewed correction; no performance claim.
next_if_negative: Save minimal failing query and investigate the index, bounds, eligibility and tie behavior.
